newsitem.title: UK: N Sea wet crude stable, refiners talk of run cuts.
newsitem.headline: N Sea wet crude stable, refiners talk of run cuts.

text.p: North Sea crude oil markets held steady on Wednesday as refiners failed to come out en-masse to buy and more talked of the possibility of cutting back on refining runs, traders said.

"The (refining) margins are not good - even for complex refineries in North West Europe so more people are considering cutting back runs," one large refiner said, adding that his company was very close to cutting back crude runs in their European refineries.
Overall CFD's firmed on the day but talked levels remained wide apart and deals were minimal.

Next week's May 27-30 dates talked around July -12/-8 cents. More action was seen on the intermonth Brent spreads where June/July traded at +6 cents but eased back later to talk around +3 cents. Brent Aug/Sept moved twice at evens.
Both Brent cargoes from the paper chains were kept - one by Phibro, the other by the Shell Group.

Talk of one million barrels of cross month (May 30-01) Brent being sold to a U.S refiner at the equivalent of July -16 cents could not be confirmed. Traders saw a trader still looking for one last cargo of June Brent to fill his early June loading VLCC destined for the U.S. Gulf.
Two cargoes of Oseberg traded - a cross month May 30-01 at the equivalent of dtd Brent +8 cents while a June 18-20 was heard moved at dated Brent +17 cents.

One company picked up one million barrels of Ekofisk loading June 7 and June 11 around Dated Brent +15-18 cents. Although only one cargo of Forties was seen available in the first decade of June, refiners did not seem to rush in to buy. Traders saw the refining value of Forties around dated Brent +25 cents.
In a quiet Mediterranean market hurting from negative refining margins, Russian Urals was pressured, with prompt barrels talked in the Dated Brent -$1.40/$1.30 area.
Later ones were a little higher.
Traders said a May 22-23 Urals was sold on Tuesday by a trader to a Spanish refiner at a distressed Dated Brent -$1.38, preceeded by a deal for a small May 27-29 loader eight cents higher.
Negative refining margins resulting from the sudden rise in North Sea Brent, which gained some $2.50 since the start of May, kept buyers at bay.
Traders said seveal Urals cargoes, mostly third decade May, were on offer and one seller said it was testing buying interest in the United States.
"I don't see that many buyers out there ...mainly because of the bad refining margins," one Italian refiner said.

In talks between Syria's state oil agency Sytrol and term lifters over June prices, the Syrians were reported to have shed three cents off their initial asking price of Dated Brent -60 cents for Syrian Light.
But buyers were far off, some offering a 90 cents discount to Dated Brent and others opting for a rollover from May's Dated Brent -82 cents.
"Dated Brent -60 cents was not very realistic," one trader said.
